SEO and WordPress support

An SEO virtual assistant prepares approved WordPress updates, checks staging and records what changed when a page goes live.

Our website content update services cover page titles, internal links, images and responsive checks. You get a preview and a list of proposed changes, so your team can approve the page before publication and check the live result afterward.

Keyword research, on-page SEO and website management

An SEO virtual assistant can prepare keyword and competitor research, on-page changes and a record of what went live. Agree the page, intended search, tools and publishing permissions before editing.

Keyword and competitor research

Collect relevant queries, group them by intent and compare competing pages or content gaps. Record the source and date and propose a focus phrase and internal links for review.

On-page and editorial checks

Prepare titles, descriptions, headings, alt text and internal links. Check article structured data and related content where in scope. Verify claims and sources with the editorial owner.

WordPress content and routine upkeep

An SEO virtual assistant can format drafts, manage pages, categories and featured images, preview on desktop and mobile and check links. Record updates, basic maintenance checks and live URLs.

Monitoring and technical handoff

Website content update services can include checking agreed search performance, links and indexing observations. Scope technical SEO, migrations and plugin or theme development with a qualified specialist.

When this support helps

A page is approved but still in a document.

Your SEO virtual assistant creates a preview, checks the layout and links, and requests sign-off.

A routine update could affect search visibility.

Flag changes to URLs, canonical tags or indexing rules for specialist review.

A live page looks wrong on mobile.

Record the viewport and steps to reproduce, then route the issue with the change history.

Read about trust and access

Planning your support

Open the topics that matter to your team. These details explain how to prepare the work, review results and handle changes.

Publish a page with a traceable release record

A sample page update changes the introduction, adds an internal link and replaces a hero image. The client wants a preview and a clear summary of the work. The update is a good pilot because it combines familiar editing with a few checks that matter on the live site.

  1. 01

    Create the preview

    The SEO virtual assistant opens the correct page in the agreed editor and confirms which fields may be changed. Use the approved brief and assets, then record the preview link. Keep any out-of-scope layout or plugin question in a separate note. Keep the preview beside the brief.

  2. 02

    Run the page checks

    Review the preview from your SEO virtual assistant against the source brief. Review the heading order, link target, image placement and supplied alternative text. Check a narrow viewport for wrapping and make sure the old and new versions are easy to compare.

  3. 03

    Publish after sign-off

    Give your SEO virtual assistant the approved version and release time. Open the live URL afterward and record which checks were repeated. If something differs from the preview, write down what changed and give the site owner a clear decision to make.

When a task needs your decision

Record the source, what you checked and who can decide. Keep blocked work visible until the next action changes.

The update changes the URL

Flag internal links, redirects and indexing implications for the site owner. Wait for the approved plan before editing the URL or publishing.

Preview and live layouts disagree

Capture the affected viewport and page state. Ask the responsible owner to decide whether to revert, fix or leave the page while the issue is investigated.

The brief asks for a plugin or theme edit

Separate the request from routine publishing. Record why it needs a specialist and keep the approved content update in its existing queue.

What we need from you

Editing permissions

Identify the editor role, pages and environments in scope. Decide who has authority to publish, change templates or make changes that affect other pages.

Definition of done

Use a checklist that includes the preview link, copy comparison, metadata when in scope, accessibility details and live checks. Give an example of an approved release record.

Rollback and escalation

Agree who can restore the previous version and where to find it. Route plugin, DNS, indexing or performance questions to the relevant specialist.

Review the results

Copy and link accuracy

Sample recent releases against their source briefs. Look for changed destinations, missing text or images that were approved in a different version.

Live verification

Confirm the release record includes the real URL and a check of the live page. Keep the preview link for context where the workspace allows it.

Recurring defects

Group repeated issues by source, such as incomplete briefs, inconsistent assets or a missing mobile check. Improve the relevant review step instead of adding a vague final reminder.

Make the next step clear

Current work

Ask your SEO virtual assistant to include the latest version, the source link and the current status. Note what was already checked and which changes were approved. Continue from the latest approved state without searching for the source or repeating a completed check.

Open decisions

List each outstanding decision, the person who can make it and the point at which the next owner should follow up. Prioritise the blocked items and ask a specific question when the next approval is due.

Time-sensitive commitments

State the time zone, the next update due and any commitments that someone has already shared. Include the agreed backup contact. Keep the next promise visible and make sure requests that cannot wait reach the correct person.

Changes to the instructions

Tell your SEO virtual assistant which rule changed, who approved it and when it starts. Keep an example that shows the difference in practice. Use the current rule and compare new work with the agreed example during the next review.

Separate routine edits from releases that need oversight.

Routine page work

Give your SEO virtual assistant a small batch of approved formatting changes, image updates and link checks. Capture the draft link and a short change note so the reviewer can compare what was requested with what will appear on the live page.

Coordinated releases

For a new campaign page, agree when the destination, analytics tags and related links will be ready to verify. Keep access and approval with the people who can sign off on the changes affecting navigation or measurement.

When something fails

Record what was changed, the pages involved and the first symptom. Agree who can restore the previous version or pause a scheduled release. A reviewer should be able to see where the issue started before deciding what to reverse.

Frequently Asked Questions

Do these updates guarantee rankings?

Search rankings are not guaranteed. Agree the publishing tasks and report the work completed.

How do you handle changes to live pages?

Define which edits need a preview or backup, who approves them and where the change is recorded.

What can you check before a page goes live?

Compare the draft with the approved brief, review headings, links and metadata, and check how the page looks at mobile and desktop widths.

What WordPress permissions are needed?

Start with the role needed to draft or edit the agreed pages. Review publishing rights, admin access and plugin changes separately.

What information goes into the release record?

Record the live URL, the work completed, the approval and any checks that still need attention after publication.

Can you make changes to a live WordPress site?

Agree which edits can go straight to review and which need staging, a rollback plan or specialist approval.
